![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `filter_by_min_severity` function currently expects `min_severity` to be a non-null string. However, if a user specifies `--drop-unknown-severity` without `--min-severity`, we should still be able to filter out unknown-severity threads while keeping all other severities. Allowing `min_severity` to be `None` enables this behavior cleanly.

```python
def filter_by_min_severity(
    threads: list[dict[str, Any]], min_severity: str | None, *, keep_unknown: bool = True
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Drop threads with severity strictly lower than min_severity.

    If min_severity is None, no minimum severity threshold is enforced.
    `unknown` threads (no Gemini priority marker) are kept by default — dropping
    them on a strict filter would silently swallow every thread Gemini didn't
    annotate, which is the wrong default for a fast-feedback loop. Pass
    keep_unknown=False to drop them anyway.
    """
    cap = SEVERITY_ORDER[min_severity] if min_severity else None
    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for t in threads:
        sev = thread_severity(t)
        if sev == "unknown":
            if keep_unknown:
                out.append(t)
            continue
        if cap is None or SEVERITY_ORDER[sev] <= cap:
            out.append(t)
    return out
```

Currently, if `--drop-unknown-severity` is passed without `--min-severity`, the filtering logic is completely skipped, meaning `--drop-unknown-severity` is silently ignored. Updating the condition to check for either option ensures that users can drop unknown-severity threads independently of a minimum severity threshold.

```suggestion
        if args.min_severity or args.drop_unknown_severity:
            before = len(threads)
            threads = filter_by_min_severity(
                threads, args.min_severity, keep_unknown=not args.drop_unknown_severity
            )
            dropped = before - len(threads)
            if dropped:
                if args.min_severity:
                    tag = " (kept unknown-severity)" if not args.drop_unknown_severity else ""
                    msg = f"--min-severity {args.min_severity}: dropped {dropped} lower-severity thread(s){tag}."
                else:
                    msg = f"Dropped {dropped} unknown-severity thread(s)."
                print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Add a test case to verify that `filter_by_min_severity` correctly drops only unknown-severity threads when `min_severity` is `None` and `keep_unknown` is `False`.

```suggestion
    def test_keep_unknown_false_drops_unmarked(self):
        items = [_sev_thread("critical"), _sev_thread(None), _sev_thread("low")]
        out = filter_by_min_severity(items, "high", keep_unknown=False)
        assert [thread_severity(t) for t in out] == ["critical"]

    def test_drop_unknown_only(self):
        items = [_sev_thread("critical"), _sev_thread(None), _sev_thread("low")]
        out = filter_by_min_severity(items, None, keep_unknown=False)
        assert [thread_severity(t) for t in out] == ["critical", "low"]
```

The help text states that `--drop-unknown-severity` is only used "When --min-severity is set". However, the implementation and tests explicitly support using `--drop-unknown-severity` on its own (without `--min-severity`) to filter out any threads that do not have an explicit severity marker.\n\nUpdating the help text to reflect this makes the CLI option much clearer and more discoverable.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

When `--min-severity` is set and `--drop-unknown-severity` is also enabled, the `dropped` count includes both threads that are below the minimum severity threshold and threads that have no severity marker (`unknown`). Referring to all of them as "lower-severity thread(s)" is misleading.\n\nSimplifying the message to "dropped {dropped} thread(s)" makes it accurate in all cases.
